label: Present Perfect
outcome: Lo studente costruisce il Present Perfect con have/has + past participle e lo usa nei tre significati core richiesti dal programma: esperienza senza tempo passato specifico, risultato collegato al presente e periodo di tempo non ancora concluso.
must_master: regular and high-frequency irregular past participles
life experience without a stated finished past time
recent or relevant result connected to now
unfinished time period at programme-appropriate level
questions with have/has before the subject
short answers at a basic school level

scope_boundary.time_adverbs: Do not systematically teach ever/never, just/already/yet or for/since here. Those belong to the later present-perfect-time-expressions topic.
scope_boundary.past_simple_contrast: Do not build a full Past Simple vs Present Perfect contrast. The dedicated Wave 1 contrast topic follows this lesson.
scope_boundary.continuous: Do not introduce Present Perfect Continuous.
scope_boundary.experience: Experience examples should avoid a specific finished past time so the learner can focus on the core meaning without prematurely teaching the full tense contrast.
scope_boundary.unfinished_time: Use transparent unfinished periods such as this week, this month or today only when the context makes it clear that the period is still open.

core_use_model.question: Has this happened in your life up to now?
Did something happen with an important result now?
core_use_model.example: I've lost my keys, so I can't get in.

core_use_model.question: Is the time period still continuing?
core_use_model.example: We've had three tests this month.

italian_learner_risks.risk: using the Past Simple form after have/has
choosing have/has from the noun nearest the verb rather than the subject
using a base verb after have/has

context_bank: things someone has experienced in their life
a lost key, broken phone or missed connection with a consequence now
tasks completed or not completed with a visible present result
things that have happened during the current week or month
messages explaining a current problem caused by a recent event

requirements: teach the two-part structure before the three core uses
show regular and irregular participles without reopening the full irregular-verb lesson
teach experience, recent result and unfinished time as distinct meanings
five scaffolded graded checks after teaching
include at least one form-focused check and at least two meaning-focused checks
do not teach the reserved time-adverb syllabus
mix structure and meaning rather than grouping all form questions together
include experience, result and unfinished-time contexts
include one question and one negative production task
avoid explicit Past Simple contrast exercises
no systematic ever/never, just/already/yet or for/since testing
include one controlled production or translation item

quality_rejections: a lesson that becomes a Past Simple vs Present Perfect comparison
systematic teaching of ever/never, just/already/yet or for/since before their dedicated topic
questions where the answer can be chosen only from a memorised signal word
Present Perfect forms without a clear present connection or experience context
using the Past Simple form after have/has in answer keys
more than two consecutive decontextualised auxiliary/participle drills
difficulty created by obscure irregular verbs rather than the target tense
